newsitem.title: INDIA: India gold, silver rise on higher world prices.
newsitem.headline: India gold, silver rise on higher world prices.

text.p: ** Gold 24 carat closes 35 rupees higher at 4,540 rupees per 10 gramme amid limited inflows and rally in the world prices
** Prices of a gold biscuit (116.64 gramme) finish 400 rupees higher at 53,100 rupees per piece after gaining 700 rupees on Thursday
** Silver (.999) ends 15 rupees higher at 6,230 rupees per kg on recovery in the world market
Higher world prices helped push up gold in the local bullion market on Friday, dealers said.
"Physical demand improved in the latter half of the day on strong overseas advices," a dealer said.
Gold opened in Europe at $323.35/$323.75 up from $319.30/$319.80 at the Thursday close in London and fixed at $323.45 up from $319.40 on Thursday.
In Bombay, the 24-carat gold gained 35 rupees to 4,540 per 10 gramme after rising 55 rupees on Thursday.
Dealers expect local demand to pick up because of the festival season ahead.
Silver (.999) closed 15 rupees higher at 6,230 rupees per kg, but off opening highs of 6,255 as fresh arrivals of imported silver dragged prices lower by close.
Silver was down by 60 rupees per kg on Thursday.
